Decide whether a word or phrase repeats no letter, ignoring case; spaces and hyphens may repeat.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/isogram) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: isogram.nomi
/// Whether no letter appears in `phrase` more than once, ignoring case.
/// Spaces, hyphens and other non-letters may repeat.
pub fn isogram?(phrase: String) -> Bool {
    letters =
        phrase
        |> String.fold_case()
        |> String.to_codepoints()
        |> Iter.filter(Codepoint.letter?)
        |> Iter.to_list()

    distinct = Iter.to_set(letters)
    Iter.count(letters) == Set.size(distinct)
}

// FILE: isogram_test.nomi
import isogram.isogram?

test "isograms" {
    cases = [
        #("empty string", "", True),
        #("isogram with only lower case characters", "isogram", True),
        #("word with one duplicated character", "eleven", False),
        #("word with one duplicated character from the end of the alphabet", "zzyzx", False),
        #("longest reported english isogram", "subdermatoglyphic", True),
        #("word with duplicated character in mixed case", "Alphabet", False),
        #("word with duplicated character in mixed case, lowercase first", "alphAbet", False),
        #("hypothetical isogrammic word with hyphen", "thumbscrew-japingly", True),
        #(
            "hypothetical word with duplicated character following hyphen",
            "thumbscrew-jappingly",
            False,
        ),
        #("isogram with duplicated hyphen", "six-year-old", True),
        #("made-up name that is an isogram", "Emily Jung Schwartzkopf", True),
        #("duplicated character in the middle", "accentor", False),
        #("same first and last characters", "angola", False),
        #("word with duplicated character and with two hyphens", "up-to-date", False),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, phrase, expected), description {
        assert isogram?(phrase) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The letters are the case-folded phrase's codepoints (`String.fold_case`,
  which is for comparing, rather than `String.to_lower`) filtered by
  `Codepoint.letter?`, which keeps every Unicode letter and drops everything
  else. `String.find_all(Regex`\pL`)` keeps the same codepoints in one stage
  instead of three, but a reader has to know `\pL`, and the filter says
  "keep the letters" in words. Filtering out `" "` and `"-"` by hand matches
  the problem text but lets any other punctuation count as a letter.
- Repeats are detected by comparing the letter count with the size of the
  letter set, rather than by folding through a set and stopping at the first
  repeat. The inputs are words, so stopping early buys nothing.
